patch.content:
#
# Copyright (c) 2015-2024 Intel Corporation
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#

# This is a minimal representation of arch/Kconfig, focusing on the problematic
# 'MAX_THREAD_BYTES' option and its direct dependencies, as the full content
# of the file is not available.

menu "Architecture Configuration"

config ARCH_HAS_USERSPACE
    bool
    help
      Select if the architecture supports user mode.

config USERSPACE
    bool "Enable user mode"
    depends on ARCH_HAS_USERSPACE
    help
      Enable user mode for threads. This allows applications to run in
      a less privileged mode, providing memory protection.

config MAX_THREAD_BYTES
    int "Maximum thread bytes"
    default 8 if USERSPACE
    default 512 # A reasonable default for kernel threads when USERSPACE is off
    help
      Maximum number of bytes for a thread. This value is used to determine
      the maximum stack size or other thread-specific memory allocation.
      If USERSPACE is enabled, it might refer to user thread limits.
      If USERSPACE is disabled, this provides a default for kernel threads.
      A segmentation fault can occur if this value is too small or zero.

endmenu
